official.deadline_note: The scholarship publishes no separate deadline: non-EU applicants are automatically considered when they apply. The controlling date is DCU's published closing date of 1 July for international applications to the 2027-28 intake; applications received after this date may not be processed for the desired programme.
official.status_note: The DCU International Scholarships for Non-EU Students 2027-28 page is published and live on dcu.ie, listing eligible programme codes and award values for the 2027-28 cycle. No separate scholarship round, opening date, or closing date is stated.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Partial: published wording is a "fee reduction on the full-time 2027-2028 Non-EU Tuition fee", with the reduction "applied directly to the student account". The reduction covers part of that academic year's tuition only; living costs, travel and other expenses are not covered.
benefits: Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences: €1,850 fee reduction (undergraduate) / €2,000 fee reduction (postgraduate) on the full-time 2027-2028 Non-EU Tuition fee
Faculty of Engineering and Computing: €5,000 fee reduction (undergraduate) / €4,400 fee reduction (postgraduate)
DCU Business School: €2,800 fee reduction (undergraduate) / €2,000 fee reduction (postgraduate)
Faculty of Science and Health: €6,100 fee reduction (undergraduate; €3,100 for DC204 BSc Athletic Therapy and Training) / €5,000 or €4,500 fee reduction (postgraduate, by programme)
Reduction in fee is applied directly to the student account
Only successful recipients are notified via email
eligibility: National of a non-EU country (open to non-EU applicants only)
Application to a full-time undergraduate or postgraduate programme on the published eligible programme list for 2027-28
Consideration is automatic on application as a non-EU student; no separate scholarship application exists
A recipient of a DCU International scholarship will not be considered for another DCU scholarship (e.g. a Merit Scholarship)
requirements: Apply to DCU as a non-EU student through the DCU Student Application Portal
Meet the academic entry requirements of the chosen programme
Meet DCU's English language requirements (or follow the holding-document process for a conditional offer)
Your programme must appear on the eligible programme list published for 2027-28
documents: Completed DCU application via the DCU Student Application Portal for an eligible 2027-28 programme
Academic transcripts and prior qualifications uploaded without password protection (DCU warns protected files delay or block assessment)
Evidence of English language proficiency from a recognised test, or a "holding document" naming the test taken and expected result date if results are pending
selection_criteria: Merit-based: DCU describes "partial merit-based scholarships to some non-EU students" and, for Humanities and Social Sciences postgraduate, "high achieving Non-EU applicants" who have received an offer
Automatic consideration of all non-EU applications to eligible programmes
coverage: Partial reduction of the full-time 2027-2028 Non-EU Tuition fee, applied directly to the student account
No coverage of living costs, travel or other expenses is published
application_method: No separate scholarship application: applicants are automatically considered when they apply to DCU as a non-EU student
Apply through DCU's Student Application Portal (dcuie2.elluciancrmrecruit.com/Apply)
official.application_route: Apply to a listed full-time DCU programme through the DCU Student Application Portal as a non-EU applicant; scholarship consideration is automatic.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to nationals of non-EU countries; no residency rule beyond non-EU status is published.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the award is exclusively for non-EU international applicants.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Programme must be on the published 2027-28 eligible list: Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, Faculty of Engineering and Computing, DCU Business School, and Faculty of Science and Health. DCU Institute of Education programmes are not listed on the page.
official.duration: Reduction applies to the full-time 2027-2028 Non-EU Tuition fee (one academic year).
official.description: Dublin City University offers partial merit-based scholarships to some non-EU students. Applicants are automatically considered for a scholarship when they apply as a non-EU student to DCU, and DCU notifies only successful recipients by email, with the fee reduction applied directly to the student account.
official.program_type: Partial merit-based tuition fee reduction for full-time undergraduate and postgraduate taught programmes in the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences, the Faculty of Engineering and Computing, DCU Business School and the Faculty of Science and Health.
official.english_requirement: IELTS Academic composite score of 6.5 or above with no less than 6.0 in any one component, achieved in one sitting and awarded within two years before the programme start (DCU Business School postgraduate programmes require 6.5 in writing and speaking; School of Communications programmes set higher writing/speaking minimums). TOEFL iBT total 92; TOEFL Home Edition is not accepted. Duolingo 120 overall with at least 110 in each subscore. PTE Academic 63 with a minimum of 59 in all components. Individual programme pages may set higher requirements.

A scholarship-specific deadline: none is published; the 1 July date is DCU's general international application closing date (the year 2027 follows from the 2027-28 intake)
Renewal of the reduction for later years of multi-year programmes: the page states the reduction only against the 2027-2028 Non-EU tuition fee
verification.notes: Award values, eligible programme codes, automatic-consideration and no-combination wording read directly from the DCU 2027-28 scholarship page; application route, 1 July international closing date and English language standards taken from DCU Registry pages, all on dcu.ie.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an automatic fee discount, not a scholarship you apply for: your only real decision is confirming your exact programme code sits on DCU's 2027-28 eligible list before you submit. Awards take €1,850 to €6,100 off the 2027-28 non-EU tuition fee depending on faculty and level, but they are partial - you must still fund the remaining tuition, Dublin living costs, flights and insurance yourself. Winners are told by email alongside their offer and nobody else hears anything, and a recipient is barred from holding any second DCU scholarship such as the Merit Scholarship.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving non-EU applicants to listed DCU undergraduate or taught postgraduate programmes who can self-fund most of their costs and want a straightforward discount on top of their offer.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your exact programme code (e.g. DC836, DC511, DC193) against the 2027-28 eligible list on the scholarship page before applying.
Upload transcripts and qualifications as unlocked, non-password-protected files - DCU warns protected documents cause delays or non-assessment.
Book a recognised English test early so the result is under two years old and achieved in one sitting.
If your English result is pending, upload the required holding document naming the test and expected result date to keep a conditional offer possible.
Submit the complete application and all documents well before 1 July; DCU warns later applications may not be processed for your desired programme.
Budget for the tuition balance after the reduction plus living costs, since the award carries no stipend.
common_rejection_risks: Choosing a programme that is not on the eligible list - for example DCU Institute of Education programmes and any unlisted code get no award.
Password-protected or unreadable uploads, which DCU states can leave the application unassessed or unsuccessful.
Missing English evidence with no holding document, so the application is not assessed until everything arrives.
Applying after 1 July or missing document deadlines, so your desired programme can no longer be processed.
Expecting an explicit rejection: only successful recipients are contacted, so silence is a no.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining balance of the non-EU tuition fee after the reduction (non-EU fees run well above the discount), plus living expenses, accommodation, health insurance and flights - none of which this award covers.
document_audit: No password-protected files: DCU explicitly warns they delay assessment or cause the application to be deemed unsuccessful.
English certificates must be awarded within two years before the programme start and from a single sitting.
Duolingo submitters must provide the verification link and share results with DCU.
TOEFL Home Edition is not accepted.
If the English test is booked but unsat, the portal's holding document is the required substitute.
Programme pages can demand higher English scores than the Registry minimum - check the specific course page.
alerts: There is no scholarship form to appeal or chase: consideration is automatic and only winners are notified by email.
Winners cannot hold another DCU scholarship - accepting this award rules out the Merit Scholarship and similar.
The page publishes the reduction only against the 2027-28 fee and says nothing about later years, so multi-year undergraduates should not assume renewal.
DCU's First Preference System treats your first portal application as your first preference; later preferences are only processed if the earlier one fails.
The award value is decided by faculty and level, not by grades you can negotiate - compare programmes on the eligible list before applying.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply through DCU's Student Application Portal as a non-EU applicant by 1 July; if admitted and selected, the award arrives by email with the offer and is credited straight to the student account.
